models.sample_description: Annual firm-year observations from Standard & Poor’s Compustat 2001 Primary-Supplementary-Tertiary, Full Coverage, and Research files with sufficient earnings-per-share and return data, linked to CRSP stock returns. Annual data span 1951–2001. The sample removes the top and bottom 1.0 percent of EPS_t/Price_(t−1) and Return_t observations in each year.
models.method_reported: The paper calls Equation (1) a regression and reports its pooled cross-sectional annual DT coefficient.
models.method_details: The underlying estimator for the pooled annual Equation (1) fit is not identified in the supplied paper text. A linear-looking equation and the term “regression” do not by themselves establish OLS.
models.equation_text: EPS_{jt} / Price_{j,t-1} = α_0 + β_0 DUM_{jt} + β_1 Return_{jt} + β_2 (DUM_{jt} × Return_{jt}) + ε_{jt}

fixed_effects.details: The pooled annual Equation (1) estimate is not accompanied by a reported fixed-effect family.

standard_errors.details: The source does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering scheme for the pooled annual Equation (1) estimate.

evidence.quote:
COORDINATOR-VERIFIED MATHEMATICAL TRANSCRIPTION (Differential-timeliness Equation (1), physical PDF page 4):
EPS_jt/Price_(j,t-1) = alpha_0 + beta_0*DUM_jt + beta_1*Return_jt + beta_2*(DUM_jt*Return_jt) + epsilon_jt. EPS is earnings per share from continuing operations. DUM=1 when Return is negative, 0 otherwise. Return is stock return computed alternatively over the fiscal year or over the twelve-month period beginning nine months before fiscal-year end. Footnote3 states raw returns and continuing-operations EPS are used unless otherwise indicated; the passage does not choose between these two timing windows for the pooled annual estimate.

estimation_procedure.description: Pooled cross-sectional estimation of Equation (1) on the annual sample; the reported annual DT coefficient β2 is 0.302. The paper does not identify a fit-specific Return window. No repeated-fit grouping is specified for this annual pooled estimate.

evidence.quote: The pooled cross-sectional DT measure (�2 in Regression (1)) of the annual sample is 0.302

preprocessing.description: Following Basu (1997), observations in the top and bottom 1.0 percent of the EPS_t/Price_(t−1) and Return_t distributions are eliminated separately each year.

evidence.quote: Observations at the top and bottom 1.0 percent of the EPSt / Pricet �1 and Returnt distributions each year are eliminated.

other.description: Unless otherwise indicated, the paper uses raw returns and earnings per share from continuing operations. It reports that market-adjusted returns and net income in place of these variables leave the results intact.

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise indicated, we present results based on raw returns and earnings per share from continuing operations. Replicating the tests using market-adjusted returns instead of raw returns and net income instead of income from continuing operations leaves the results intact.

review_notes: The supplied verified reading transcription and rendered physical PDF page 4 support all Equation (1) terms and Price_(j,t−1) timing; the equation is complete.
The final annual sample is 131,920 firm-years, not the 14,383-firm count. The sample description and annual-period trimming are supported on reading page 5.

Underlying estimator, standard-error procedure, fixed effects and weights are not reported for this fit. Only the estimator uncertainty is material to status; return-window selection is fit-specific and unclear.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
IV. SAMPLE AND DATA
Most of the empirical analyses in this paper rely on a sample consisting of all firms
on Standard & Poor’s Compustat 2001 database (Primary-Supplementary-Tertiary, Full
Coverage, and Research files) that have sufficient earnings per share and return data to
perform the tests. Earnings data are available annually over the years 1951 to 2001 and
quarterly from 1962 to 2001. Returns are obtained from the Center for Research in Security
Prices (CRSP) data file.

The initial sample of annual data consists of 14,616 firms and 136,887 firm-years.
Following Basu (1997), we eliminate extreme observations of the earnings per share and
return distributions every year. <sup>4</sup> This results in a final sample of 14,383 firms and 131,920
firm-years.
